questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An atomic substance A of molar mass 12 g mol–1 has a cubic crystal structure with edge length of 300 pm. The no. of atoms present in one unit cell of A is

(Nearest integer)

Given the density of A is 3.0 g m m-1 and NAA=6.02×1023 mol-1
questions.solution:
The density of crystal can be calculated as follows,

ρ=Z×MNA×a3

ρ=density of the unit cell

Z=Effective atomic number

M=Molar mass

NA=Avogadro's number

a=Edge length of the unit cell

3=Z×126.02×1023×(3)3×10-24

Z=6.02×10-1×274=4

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct relationships between unit cell edge length ‘<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>’ and radius of sphere ‘<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></math>’ for face-centred and body-centred cubic structures respectively are:
questions.solution:
A face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell contains a component in the center of each face in addition to those at the corners of the cube. The atoms touch each other along the face diagonal.

For  FCC:  a2=4r

a=22r

A body-centered cubic (bcc) unit cell contains a component in the center of the cube in addition to those at the corners of the cube. The atoms touch each other along the body diagonal.

For BCC : a3=4r

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Number of crystal systems from the following where body centred unit cell can be found, is _____.

Cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, hexagonal, rhombohedral, monoclinic, triclinic
questions.solution:
Bravais Lattice refers to the 14 different 3-dimensional configurations into which atoms can be arranged in crystals. The smallest group of symmetrically aligned atoms which can be repeated in an array to make up the entire crystal is called a unit cell. Crystal systems where body centred unit cell can be found are Cubic, orthorhombic and tetragonal

Hence, correct answer is 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A compound is formed by two elements X and Y. The element Y forms cubic close packed arrangement and those of element X occupy one third of the tetrahedral voids. What is the formula of the compound?
questions.solution:
Atoms of Element Y, are present in cubic close packing. In cubic close packing the number of atoms per unit cell is 4.

So, the effective number of element Y, per unit cell is 4

Element X, are present at one third of the tetrahedral voids.

Number of tetrahedral void =Twice the number of atoms in unit cell

Number of atoms of Element X are present unit cell =13×8=83

X : Y83 : 42   : 3

Formula of the compound =X2Y3

M=Molar mass

NA=Avogadro's number

a=Edge length

dFCCdBCC=4×MwNA×(2)32×MwNA×(2.5)3=3.90

questions.q:
Which of the following represents the lattice structure of A0.95O containing A2+, A3+ and O2– ions?

A.

B.

C.

Applying the electrical neutrality principle in metal deficiency defect.

One A2+ is missing then two A2+ ions are converted into A3+ ion so 0.05 A2+ ion are missing and 0.05×2 A2+ ion are converted in A3+ ion so for each O2- ion total A2+ ion 0.85 and A3+ ion is 0.1.

Hence, A satisfies the condition.

The metal <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> can exist in two oxidation states <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. In the sample of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>83</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn></mrow></msub></math>, the percentage of metal ions existing in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> oxidation state is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math>. questions.solution:
Let number of ions of M+2=x

Thus, as net charge has to be zero, M+3=0.83-x

⇒2x+3(0.83-x)+1(-2)=0

⇒2x+2.49-3x-2=0

∴x=0.49

%M2+ ions =0.490.83×100=59.03

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The incorrect statement about the imperfections in solids is
options: Schottky defect decreases the density of the substance.
Frenkel defect does not alter the density of the substance.
Interstitial defect increases the density of the substance.
Vacancy defect increases the density of the substance.
questions.solution:
Frenkel Defect: This defect is shown by ionic solids. The smaller ion (usually cation) is dislocated from its normal site to an interstitial site. It creates a vacancy defect at its original site and an interstitial defect at its new location. Frenkel defect is also called dislocation defect. It does not change the density of the solid. In all other defects there is a change in the density.

In Schottky defect equal number of cation and anion are missing from their position so, it decreases the density of the substance.

In Interstitial defect extra atoms are present at interstitial position so, it increases the density of the substance.

Due to vacancy defect density of the substance will decrease. since atoms are missing from their positions.

If both <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>AB</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> weigh equally, then the atomic weight of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is____times of atomic weight of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>.
questions.solution:
Given: Molar mass of A2B=AB3

∴ 2A+B=A+3BA→Atomicwt. of AB→Atomicwt. of B

⇒A=2 B

∴ atomic wt. of A is 2 times of atomic wt. of B Integer answer is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a solid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AB</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> atoms are in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ccp</mi></math> arrangement and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> atoms occupy all the octahedral sites. If two atoms from the opposite faces are removed, then the resultant stoichiometry of the compound is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></msub></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> is [nearest integer]
questions.solution:
A forms ccp structure that means number of A atoms per unit cell →4

B atoms per unit cell →4 (Octahedral voids), as number of octahedral voids will be equal to number of atoms per unit cell.

A removed =2×12=1

A left =4-1=3

Formula becomes A3B4

x=3.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : Frenkel defects are vacancy as well as interstitial defects.
Statement II : Frenkel defect leads to colour in ionic solids due to presence of F-centres.

Choose the most appropriate answer for the statements from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
questions.solution: A Frenkel defect is another form of a point defect which is created when an atom or cation leaves its original place in the lattice structure to create a vacancy while occupying another interstitial position within the solid crystal. Frenkel defect is dislocation defect, it is not interstitial defect, and it is not responsible for colour of solid.

Given below are two statements. One is labelled as
Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Reason R: The viscosity of glass decreases on melting.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is true but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is false

explanation of A.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is false but <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is true.

questions.solution:
AgBr can exhibit both Schottky and Frenkel defect.

Schottky defect in AgBr is exhibited due to the precipitation of both cations and anions. In AgBr, Ag+ ion is small in size and when removed from the lattice point, they can occupy the interstitial sites and, hence, shows both Frenkel and Schottky defects.

The appearance of colour in alkali metal halides is generally due to F-centres. F centers in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ produce a band of optical absorption towards the blue end of visible

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many unit cells are present in a cubeshaped ideal crystal of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ of mass $1.00 \mathrm{~g}$ ? [Atomic masses: $\mathrm{Na}=23, \mathrm{Cl}=35.5$ ]
questions.solution:
Number of formulas in cube shaped crystals $=\frac{1.0}{58.5} \times 6.02 \times 10^{23}$ since in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ type of structure 4 formula units form a cell
$\therefore$ unit cells $=\frac{1.0 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23}}{58.5 \times 4}=2.57 \times 10^{21}$ unit cells.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Na and Mg crystallize in BCC and FCC type crystals respectively, then the number of atoms of Na and Mg present in the unit cell of their respective crystal is
questions.solution:
BCC - points are at corners and one in the centre of the unit cell
Number of atoms per unit cell $=8 \times \frac{1}{8}+1=2$
FCC - points are at the corners and also centre of the six faces of each cell
Number of atoms per unit cell $=8 \times \frac{1}{8}+6 \times \frac{1}{2}=4$
